questions.title: Chamber Entrance: Pedestal Lock
questions.prompt: The ancient pedestal lock demands energy. Assign 50 gold coins to the variable 'gold' to activate the mechanism.
questions.code_snippet:
# Store 50 gold coins in the variable 'gold'
gold = ____
questions.explanation: In Python, assigning a whole number without quotes creates an integer (int). You do not need to declare types like in C++ or Java.
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: Simply assign the raw numeric value: '50'. No quotation marks or type keywords are needed!

questions.title: Altar of Transmutation: Key Type
questions.prompt: To forge the key that fits the chest's keyhole, assign the string 'Gold' to the variable 'key_type'.
questions.code_snippet:
# Complete the assignment with string 'Gold'
key_type = ____
questions.explanation: Text values in Python are strings (str) and must be enclosed in single or double quotes, e.g. 'Gold'.
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: Any text without quotes is treated as a variable name. Wrap 'Gold' in quotes!

questions.title: Rune of Identification: Gem Weight
questions.prompt: Alex inspects a glowing gem on the pedestal: 'gem_weight = 3.75'. What data type is returned by type(gem_weight)?
questions.explanation: In Python, numbers with decimal places are stored as 'float' (floating-point). Python has no separate 'double' type.
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: Notice the decimal in 3.75. In Python, decimal numbers belong to the 'float' type!

questions.title: The Vault Gate: Opening the Chest
questions.prompt: Arrange the code blocks in proper order to set the chest state to True, check the condition, and command Alex to open it!
questions.explanation: In Python, booleans must be capitalized (True / False). We assign the boolean variable first, evaluate it with 'if', and execute the indented block.
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: State the boolean variable first ('True'), then the 'if' condition, followed by the indented action!
